content.title: About
content.content: Carnitas are a traditional Mexican dish of slowly braised pork seasoned with spices, lime, and orange juice. The meat is cooked until tender, then crisped to a golden crust, delivering a savory, slightly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the Spanish word “carnitas,” meaning “little pieces of meat.”
Traditionally the dish is cooked in large copper pots called “cazos.”
In Mexico carnitas are commonly served in tacos, burritos, and with salsa.
Pork shoulder or butt, rich in connective tissue, is usually used to keep the meat juicy.
Carnitas are often topped with fresh cilantro, onion, and lime.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Pork provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports the nervous system and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from pork helps transport oxygen throughout the body.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 participates in amino‑acid metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Carnitas are made from fatty cuts; those monitoring fat intake should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Added soy sauce or salt can raise sodium, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked pork may harbor pathogens; ensure internal temperature reaches at least 71 °C (160 °F).

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pork.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve carnitas in soft corn or flour tortillas, topped with fresh onion, cilantro, guacamole, salsa, and a squeeze of lime. It can also be used as a filling for burritos, salads, or enjoyed as a main dish with rice and beans.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked carnitas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
